                                   SOAH DOCKET NO. 473-26-16349
                                      PUC DOCKET NO. 59475

JOINT APPLICATION OF ONCOR                                             §
ELECTRIC DELIVERY COMPANY LLC                                          §
AND LCRA TRANSMISSION                                                  §
SERVICES CORPORATION TO                                                §      BEFORE THE STATE OFFICE
AMEND THEIR CERTIFICATES OF                                            §
CONVENIENCE AND NECESSITY                                              §                            OF
FOR THE BELL COUNTY EAST                                               §
SWITCH TO BIG HILL SUBSTATION                                          §     ADMINISTRATIVE HEARINGS
765-KV TRANSMISSION LINE                                               §
PROJECT IN BELL, BURNET,                                               §
CONCHO, CORYELL, LAMPASAS,                                             §
LLANO, MASON, MCCULLOCH,                                               §
MENARD, MILAM, MILLS, SAN                                              §
SABA, SCHLEICHER, TOM GREEN,                                           §
AND WILLIAMSON COUNTIES                                                §


      INTERVENOR THE ESTATE AND TRUST OF JOYCE ANN RUNDBERG’S
                            REPLY BRIEF

                                             I. INTRODUCTION
        Applicants’ Initial Post-Hearing Brief confirms, rather than rebuts, the Estate’s case against
Link F41 as routed across Tract 2641.1. Applicants concede that all 122 filed routes are “viable
and constructible,” that they “do not object to the selection of any filed route or constructible
combination of forward-progressing alternative route links,” and that route selection is “a
balancing of factors” under PURA § 37.056(c). Those concessions mean the Commission may
select an alternative that avoids the disproportionate, cumulative harm to Tract 2641.1 without any
cost to reliability or constructability.

        What Applicants do not do is engage the tract-specific record. Their brief never weighs the
cumulative burden already imposed on Tract 2641.1 by the Ronald Reagan taking and the
Schwertner easement; never addresses the F41 centerline’s crossing of the back stock tank; never
accounts for the confirmed Texas Horned Lizard habitat and harvester-ant colonies along the
centerline; never identifies the Holy Trinity Catholic Church and Cemetery, the Islamic Center of
Jarrell, or the historic timber road; and never demonstrates that the routing analysis was performed
to certified 765-kV standards. Applicants instead defer environmental and cultural review to post-
approval agency consultation and rely on a general notice finding that does not reach the Estate’s


                      Intervenor The Estate and Trust of Joyce Ann Rundberg Reply Brief • Page 1 of 5


                                                                               Doc ID: ccae1dad6a260f3383bbc7cc0f6d9622b180082b
 distinct route-change objection. The Commission should reject F41 across Tract 2641.1 as filed
and direct a bona fide alternatives analysis; in the alternative, it should impose the binding
conditions the Estate has requested.

II. APPLICANTS’ OWN CONCESSIONS REMOVE ANY OBSTACLE TO AVOIDING
                           TRACT 2641.1
       Applicants represent that any of the 122 routes “are viable and constructible” and that they
“do not object to the selection of any filed route or constructible combination of forward-
progressing alternative route links.” Applicants’ Initial Post-Hearing Brief at 40, 59. By
Applicants’ own admission, then, an alignment that spares Tract 2641.1 of a third major
encumbrance is available and buildable, and Applicants will construct it. Because Applicants are
indifferent as among constructible routes, the landowner-protective standard of PURA § 37.056(c)
governs the choice—and that standard weighs decisively against stacking a 765-kV corridor onto
a tract already reduced by a 10.36-acre highway taking and a perpetual water-utility easement.

  III. APPLICANTS’ “BALANCING, NOT SCORING” ARGUMENT IGNORES THE
                      CUMULATIVE-IMPACT RECORD
       Applicants argue that route selection is “not a math question” and reject any weighted
scoring methodology. Applicants’ Initial Post-Hearing Brief at 41. The Estate has not asked for a
scoring formula. The Estate’s point is that a reasoned balancing—the very exercise Applicants
endorse—must account for the cumulative burden on Tract 2641.1, and Applicants’ analysis does
not. Applicants’ route comparison reports system-wide totals for entire routes; it does not weigh
the pre-existing Ronald Reagan taking and Schwertner easement as aggravating factors that make
an additional encumbrance on Tract 2641.1 more harmful than the same encumbrance on an
unburdened parcel. The Estate’s Demonstrative Exhibit 29 sets out the factor-by-factor analysis
under § 37.056(c) and 16 TAC § 25.101 and stands unrebutted. A balancing that treats Tract 2641.1
as if it were undisturbed is not a balancing of the actual record.

     IV. DEFERRING THREATENED-SPECIES REVIEW TO POST-APPROVAL
               CONSULTATION DOES NOT SATISFY § 37.056(c)
       Applicants respond to the environmental record by pointing to standard ordering
paragraphs and to consultation with the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service under the Endangered
Species Act that, by their own account, will occur only “following the Commission’s approval” of
the Project. Applicants’ Initial Post-Hearing Brief at 55–57. They further note that TPWD filed no


                     Intervenor The Estate and Trust of Joyce Ann Rundberg Reply Brief • Page 2 of 5


                                                                              Doc ID: ccae1dad6a260f3383bbc7cc0f6d9622b180082b
 comments in this docket and that its recommendations are “already part of Applicants’ standard
practice.” None of this answers the routing question. Section 37.056(c) requires the effect on the
environment to be weighed when the route is selected, not studied after the fact. The Estate’s
unrebutted testimony confirms Texas Horned Lizard habitat—a Texas-listed Threatened species—
on the F41 centerline, two active native harvester-ant colonies (the lizard’s primary prey) in the
line’s direct path, and the centerline’s crossing of the back stock tank. Applicants conducted no
site-specific biological survey of Tract 2641.1 before filing. Selecting the route first and surveying
for threatened species later inverts the statutory sequence and risks the very habitat destruction the
law is meant to prevent.

V. POST-APPROVAL THC COORDINATION DOES NOT CURE THE OMISSION OF
          CULTURAL RESOURCES FROM THE ROUTING RECORD
       Applicants state that “[a] cultural resources survey plan will be developed with the THC
for the Project,” again after Commission approval. Applicants’ Initial Post-Hearing Brief at 56. A
post-approval survey plan does not answer the Estate’s objection: Applicants’ cultural-resource
assessment never identified the Holy Trinity Catholic Church and Cemetery (8626 FM 1105), the
Islamic Center of Jarrell (9401 FM 1105) directly across FM 1105, or the unpreserved historic
timber road along the southern and southwestern borders of Tract 2641.1. Cultural resources that
are never identified cannot be weighed in route selection. Deferring identification until after the
route is chosen defeats the purpose of considering these resources under § 37.056(c).

    VI. THE ORDER NO. 7 NOTICE FINDING DOES NOT ANSWER THE ROUTE-
                 CHANGE-WITHOUT-NOTICE OBJECTION
       Applicants rely on the ALJs’ finding in SOAH Order No. 7 that their statutory mailing
notice was sufficient, and emphasize that they mailed notice on an intentionally overinclusive basis
to owners within 520 feet of the centerline. That finding addresses whether Applicants satisfied
the mailing requirements of 16 TAC § 22.52(a). It does not reach the Estate’s separate objection:
that the F41 alignment presented at Oncor’s June 2025 landowner meeting differed from the
alignment in the filed application—shifting to the path that now crosses the back stock tank and
confirmed threatened-species habitat—without notice of the change. Applicants’ statement that
“the Parties did not reach an agreement on a route that relies on modifications to the route segments
as noticed in the Application” concerns post-filing modifications under 16 TAC § 22.52(a)(3)(D);
it does not rebut the pre-filing route change Brenda Rundberg described in unrebutted testimony.


                     Intervenor The Estate and Trust of Joyce Ann Rundberg Reply Brief • Page 3 of 5


                                                                              Doc ID: ccae1dad6a260f3383bbc7cc0f6d9622b180082b
 The Commission should treat that change as a factor weighing against approval of F41 in its filed
alignment.

  VII. APPLICANTS DO NOT REBUT THE UNRESOLVED 765-kV ENGINEERING
                            DEFICIENCY
       Applicants’ brief does not establish that the routing and design analysis underlying F41
was conducted to certified 765-kV standards rather than the 345-kV standards the Estate identified.
The choice of voltage determines easement width, tower height, conductor clearances, and the
radius of significant EMF exposure. A routing analysis premised on the wrong design standard
systematically understates the land burden and proximity impacts on every affected tract, including
Tract 2641.1. Because the record does not confirm a qualified, independent 765-kV engineering
validation, the Commission cannot find on this record that F41 as routed reflects the true land
impact of the Project, and any approval should be conditioned on independent engineering
validation at certified 765-kV standards.

  VIII. THE REQUESTED CONDITIONS ARE MODEST AND CONSISTENT WITH
                     APPLICANTS’ OWN POSITION
       Applicants state that they do not object to the Commission’s standard ordering paragraphs
requiring environmental compliance and agency coordination. The conditions the Estate requests,
should F41 be approved across Tract 2641.1, are of the same character and should be imposed: a
TPWD-coordinated threatened-species survey with any required mitigation or permits; a qualified
cultural-resource survey addressing the historic timber road and the church and cemetery;
engineering validation at certified 765-kV standards; construction measures protective of the
property’s four water wells and the back stock tank; pre-construction re-engagement with Brenda
Rundberg using specific, plain-language notice of the final approved alignment; and a land-
damage assessment that accounts for cumulative easement impacts and severance damages to the
agricultural remainder. The Estate does not oppose transmission infrastructure as a matter of
principle; it asks only that F41 not be approved across Tract 2641.1 on an incomplete record.

                                IX. CONCLUSION AND PRAYER
       Applicants’ brief establishes that an alternative to F41 across Tract 2641.1 is available,
constructible, and unopposed by Applicants. The Estate respectfully requests that the Commission:
(1) decline to approve Link F41 across Tract 2641.1 in its filed alignment and require Applicants



                    Intervenor The Estate and Trust of Joyce Ann Rundberg Reply Brief • Page 4 of 5


                                                                             Doc ID: ccae1dad6a260f3383bbc7cc0f6d9622b180082b
 to present a bona fide route-alternative analysis accounting for the cumulative burden of the Ronald
Reagan taking and Schwertner easement, the confirmed Texas Horned Lizard habitat and
harvester-ant colonies, the back stock-tank crossing, the Holy Trinity Catholic Church and
Cemetery, and the unpreserved historic timber road; (2) in the alternative, condition any approval
as set forth above and in the Estate’s Initial Brief; (3) find that the unnoticed pre-filing route change
is a procedural irregularity warranting heightened scrutiny of the F41 routing determination; (4)
condition any CCN amendment on independent engineering validation at certified 765-kV
standards; and (5) grant such other and further relief to which the Estate is justly entitled.

                                                            Respectfully submitted,
